official.description_text:
Postdoc in Smart BMS, PVT Integration and Lifecycle Data Systems
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Job description
The project develops interoperable digital and control solutions for positive energy buildings and energy communities. The postdoctoral researcher will integrate building management systems (BMS), programmable logic controllers (PLCs), HVAC components, sensors, thermal storage and renewable technologies, including photovoltaic-thermal (PVT) systems. Research includes model-based and predictive control, hardware and software onboarding, and experimental validation in real buildings. A central contribution is a reusable digital infrastructure using semantic models and standardised interfaces to connect design, product, installation, commissioning and operational data across the building lifecycle. The researcher will also assess whole-system sustainability through energy, carbon and life-cycle performance analysis, considering operational benefits, embodied impacts and circularity. Work combines technical modelling, data integration and collaboration with building owners and technology providers. The postdoc reasearcher will contribute to 20% of teaching and department duties.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
PhD in building automation, control engineering, building energy systems, energy informatics or a related field.
Knowledge of BMS, PLCs, HVAC components, sensors and energy system modelling.
Experience in control algorithm development, simulation, software integration or automation research.
Strong scientific communication skills in English, as this will be required in day-to-day work.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline
Hands-on BMS commissioning, sensor deployment, embedded control and BACnet/Modbus integration.
Experience with PVT, heat pumps, thermal storage and renewable system control.
Semantic modelling, ontologies, BIM, digital twins and lifecycle data interoperability.
Experience with LCA, EPDs, embodied carbon or sustainability assessment of integrated systems.
Awareness of diversity and equal opportunity issues, with specific focus on gender equality
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Join us at KTH
KTH shapes the future through education, research and innovation. As a leading international technical university, we play an active role in advancing the transition towards a sustainable society. At KTH, you have the opportunity to grow and develop in a creative and dynamic environment, with good working conditions and attractive benefits. Equality, diversity and equal opportunities are essential to quality and form an integral part of KTH’s core values as a university and public authority.
Learn more about our benefits and what it's like to work and grow at KTH.

To apply for the position
Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:
CV including relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Copy of diplomas and grades from your previous university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any of these languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally two pages long.
Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
About the employment
The position offered is for, at the most, two years.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position at KTH integrating building management systems (BMS), PLCs, HVAC, sensors, and renewable technologies (particularly PVT systems). Focus is on model-based/predictive control, hardware-software integration, digital infrastructure for the building lifecycle, and whole-system sustainability assessment. Includes 20% teaching and departmental duties.

thematic_fit.rationale: Negligible thematic alignment. The posting is about building energy systems integration, control engineering, and lifecycle data management. No mention of immersive systems, human-centred design, spatial learning, collaboration, or XR. The researcher's core themes (human-centred XR, collaborative immersive systems, spatial cognition, wayfinding) are absent from the role's scope.

methodological_fit.rationale: Limited methodological fit. The researcher has user-studies, experimental-design, and quantitative-research skills. The posting emphasizes control algorithm development, simulation, BMS commissioning, and data integration—technical infrastructure work. No user-centred evaluation, human factors assessment, or learning outcomes measurement is mentioned. The posting does not require HCI methodology.

growth_value.rationale: Minimal growth value for target identity. This role would develop expertise in building automation and energy systems engineering, which does not close gaps in human-centred XR research, spatial cognition, immersive systems design, or collaborative methodologies. It represents a pivot into infrastructure engineering, not immersive HCI.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a strong institution in Stockholm, Sweden (preferred country, Europe). Funding appears stable (2-year postdoc). However, the research group focus (building energy systems, sustainability) has no documented overlap with human-centred immersive systems or HCI. The 20% teaching load is a positive for academic development, but the research mission is misaligned. No pathway to target identity research.

missing_skills: building automation (BMS, PLCs, BACnet/Modbus not in taxonomy)
control algorithm development (simulation tools: MATLAB, Modelica, etc.)
eligibility_flags: Requires PhD; researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress). Must be conferred before employment decision.
Posting notes: 'A doctoral degree...obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline' is preferred. Timeline unclear if researcher graduates in 2026.
Security clearance mentioned (Protective Security Act 2018:585). Applicability and timing unknown; flagged as ambiguous in posting.
risks: Domain mismatch: building energy systems engineering vs. human-centred immersive systems research. No overlap in research culture or methodology.

Heavy technical infrastructure focus (BMS commissioning, control algorithms, data interoperability) rather than human-centred evaluation. Researcher's strength is in user studies and spatial learning outcomes, not control system integration.
KTH's School of Architecture and Built Environment is unlikely to have HCI, XR, or immersive systems research groups. Limited community fit and no research network to support future trajectory.
Taking this role would consume 2 years and delay or redirect PhD plans away from target research direction.
Skill gap in control engineering, BMS/PLC integration, and energy system modeling.
